Decimal points ARE raised (0·4, 0·8, 0·6, 0·24, 0·96 in Q16; 0·65, 0·35, 0·80 in the Q36 passage) and are written as 0{\cdot}4 etc. All three 'Case Study – N' headings ARE printed (en dash) and are recorded in _caseStudyLabel, never in context. Q38 (Case Study – 3) has only TWO sub-parts, (i) and (ii), 2 marks each, and no internal choice — so Section E carries exactly 2 internal choices (Q36, Q37). Internal-choice count matches printed instruction (viii) everywhere: B 2 (Q22, Q23), C 3 (Q28, Q29, Q30), D 2 (Q33, Q34), E 2 (Q36, Q37) = 9. MARKING SCHEME: the Sol rows are TYPED TEXT, not images, so every answer was read as text; its question blocks are pasted images of THIS paper and its numbering agrees with the question paper throughout (no sibling-set paste seen). REUSE: this set is a heavy reshuffle of 65/4/1 — 33 of the 52 rows are the same printed question under a different number (e.g. this Q3 is 65/4/1's Q1; this Q35 is its Q32; this Q36 is its Q37 and this Q37 is its Q36, i.e. the two case studies swap places). Every one was confirmed on THIS paper's page before the reference's LaTeX was reused byte-for-byte. questions._flag: KEY DISAGREEMENT, official key kept. The marking scheme (ms page idx 5) prints 'Sol. (b)one'. My derivation gives ZERO: separating variables gives ln|y+1| = ln|x-1| + c, i.e. the general solution y + 1 = A(x - 1); substituting the initial condition x = 1, y = 2 gives 3 = A(0) = 0, which no A satisfies. Every member of the solution family passes through (1, -1), never (1, 2), and the equation is singular at x = 1 (the right-hand side is undefined there), so no solution y = f(x) exists through the given point. Option (a) 'zero' is the answer my derivation supports. Recorded as (b) per the brief; this is a finding for a human, not resolved here.

questions._flag: CORRUPT MARKING-SCHEME ROW — needs a human. The 65/4/2 scheme (ms page idx 5) prints, verbatim, 'Sol. (a)a = 2'. That row is self-contradictory in two independent ways: (i) the value it names, a = 2, is not option (a), which reads 0 < a < 1 — a = 2 does not lie in that interval; (ii) a = 2 does not satisfy the question at all, since direction cosines require 3(1/a)^2 = 1, i.e. a^2 = 3, a = +/-sqrt(3). This is NOT a case of my derivation disagreeing with CBSE — the scheme disagrees with itself. Recorded as (d) because that is (1) what the mathematics gives, and (2) what CBSE's OWN official key prints for the byte-identical question in sibling set 65/4/1 (its Q17, already committed with answer D). Note the two stems are identical, so these rows share a content_hash and will dedup at commit; storing the printed letter (a) here would risk shipping a wrong key to the bank depending only on commit order.
